# Udāna-aṭṭhakathā (Atk S0503a)
**ID:** Atk S0503a
**Section:** Aṭṭhakathā Khuddakanikāya (atk-s05)
**Collection:** Atthakatha-Suttas
**Title (Pali):** Udāna-aṭṭhakathā
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Udāna-aṭṭhakathā*, also known as *Paramatthadīpanī* (or *Paramatthadīpanī I*), is the canonical commentary on the *Udāna* within the Khuddakanikāya, attributed to the commentator Dhammapāla (ca. sixth century) [Phaengcharoen 2006; Powers 2009]. The work engages in extensive doctrinal exposition and textual reconciliation; for example, it undertakes the resolution of internal textual contradictions observed by the commentator [Adikaram 1946]. Among commentarial texts, it is notable for offering a specific definition and analysis of *vāsanā* (the persistent imprint or habit-energy of defilements) in the context of the elder Pilinda Vaccha [Endo 1997]. It also provides an elaborate exegesis of epithets of the Buddha, such as *sugata*—drawing on sources beyond those used by Buddhaghosa in the *Visuddhimagga*—and elaborates on the residual strands of past karma (*kammapiloti*) that accounted for the Buddha's physical suffering [Endo 1997; MacCormack]. Dhammapāla's treatment in this work was regarded as authoritative in the southern transmission, being cited by name alongside the *Itivuttaka-aṭṭhakathā* for detailed exposition in other commentaries such as the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* [Endo 1997].
Text-reuse analysis reveals extensive sharing across the Pali commentarial and sub-commentarial corpus, comprising 62,049 matching segments with 544 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Its most substantial internal reuse occurs with other commentaries of the same tradition, notably Dhammapāla's *Itivuttaka-aṭṭhakathā* (1,739 matches, over 226,000 characters; longest segment §454_3–513_2 ↔ §574_3–630_2), the *Vinayapiṭake Sāratthadīpanī-ṭīkā*, the *Mūlapaṇṇāsa-aṭṭhakathā*, and the *Paṭisambhidāmagga-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. No cross-language DharmaNexus matches with Sanskrit, Chinese, or Tibetan corpora meet the reporting threshold of score ≥10 [DharmaNexus]. The commentary has been published in modern scholarly editions by F. L. Woodward and Peter Masefield for the Pali Text Society, as well as in the Hewavitarana Sinhala-script edition [Adikaram 1946; Phaengcharoen 2006; Powers 2009].
**Parallels and text reuse**

- Text reuse within the Pali corpus (DharmaNexus): Itivuttaka-aṭṭhakathā (Atk S0504a) (§454_3–513_2 ↔ §574_3–630_2); Vinayapiṭake Sāratthadīpanī-ṭīkā (tatiyo bhāgo) (Tika Vin02t) (§1547_5–1614_2 ↔ §1498_17–1566_3); Majjhimanikāye Mūlapaṇṇāsa-aṭṭhakathā (Atk S0201a) (§1135_1–1139_4 ↔ §667–673_4); Paṭisambhidāmagga-aṭṭhakathā (Atk S0517a) (§452_9–458_1 ↔ §874_3–878_3); Dīghanikāye Sīlakkhandhavaggaṭṭhakathā (Atk S0101a) (§452_9–458_1 ↔ §398_2–402_3); Aṅguttaranikāye Ekakanipāta-aṭṭhakathā (Atk S0401a) (§452_9–458_2 ↔ §429_2–433_4); Aṅguttaranikāye Aṭṭhakanipāta-ṭīkā (Tika S0404t) (§864–895_2 ↔ §318_2–342_1); Majjhimanikāye Mūlapaṇṇāsa-ṭīkā (Tika S0201t) (§136_0–139_4 ↔ §175_0–176_11)
**Sources**

- [Adikaram 1946] E. W. Adikaram, Early History of Buddhism in Ceylon (1946) — Discusses textual reconciliation in the commentary and cites the Hewavitarana edition.
- [DharmaNexus] DharmaNexus text-reuse database — Provides data on Pali-internal text reuse and lack of cross-language matches.

- [MacCormack] MacCormack, Buddhism and State in Seventeenth-Century Tibet — Notes Dhammapāla's explanation of the Buddha's suffering via kammapiloti.
